prompt_text: I need help choosing a health insurance plan in Kansas City. Which specific brokers should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
competitors_mentioned: Spring Venture Group — Kansas City area
Missouri Department of Commerce and Insurance
engine_stated_criteria: “Are you licensed in Missouri, Kansas, or both?”
“Which carriers are you appointed with for my type of coverage?”
“Can you show me Marketplace/on-exchange plans as well as off-exchange plans?”
answer_verbatim:
Kansas City spans two states, so the right broker depends heavily on whether you live/work on the Missouri or Kansas side and whether you need **individual/family, Medicare, or employer coverage**. I would start with these organizations:

| If you need… | Call | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Employer coverage / small-to-mid-size business** | **Bukaty Companies — Leawood, KS** | Long-established Kansas City employee-benefits brokerage. A good first call for employer medical, dental, vision, HSA/HRA, and compliance help. Particularly worth calling if you want hands-on local service rather than just an online quote. |
| **Employer coverage / larger or more complex business** | **Lockton — Kansas City, MO** | Kansas City-based national benefits brokerage with strong capabilities for larger groups, self-funded plans, HR/benefits administration, and complex network or pharmacy-cost analysis. It may be more than a very small employer needs, but it is a strong comparison point. |
| **Medicare Advantage, Medigap, or Part D** | **Spring Venture Group — Kansas City area** | Kansas City-based Medicare insurance distribution company. Ask specifically whether the agent can compare multiple carriers and whether they offer both Medicare Advantage and Medigap options—not just one type of product. |
| **Individual/family ACA coverage, self-employed coverage, or early-retiree coverage** | Use **HealthCare.gov’s “Find Local Help”** directory for your ZIP code and call two Marketplace-certified brokers listed there | This is usually better than picking a generic “health insurance” broker. A Marketplace-certified broker can compare ACA plans, premium tax credits, and local provider networks. Both Missouri and Kansas residents generally use HealthCare.gov for Marketplace coverage. |

## My practical recommendation

### If you are buying coverage for yourself or your family
Do **not** make your first call to a large employer-benefits firm such as Lockton. Instead:

1. Go to **HealthCare.gov/find-local-help**.
2. Enter your ZIP code.
3. Call **two independent agents/brokers** listed as Marketplace-certified.
4. Also compare the result directly on HealthCare.gov before enrolling.

That route matters because an individual-policy broker may only be appointed with certain carriers, while the Marketplace will show the full set of available ACA options and any subsidy you qualify for.

### If you are shopping for Medicare
Before talking to a broker, get a neutral comparison from:

- **Kansas SHICK** if you live in Kansas: **1-800-860-5260**
- **Missouri CLAIM** if you live in Missouri: **1-800-390-3330**

They are not insurance sales brokers; they provide unbiased Medicare counseling. Then use a broker such as Spring Venture Group or another local independent Medicare broker if you want enrollment help.

### If you are selecting benefits for a business
Call **Bukaty** and **Lockton** for a comparison. If you have fewer than roughly 10–20 employees, tell them that immediately and ask whether they serve groups your size; some large consultancies focus more heavily on mid-market and larger employers.

## Questions to ask every broker

Use these exact questions:

1. **“Are you licensed in Missouri, Kansas, or both?”**  
   Use the state where the policyholder lives or where your business is headquartered.

2. **“Which carriers are you appointed with for my type of coverage?”**  
   A broker who represents more carriers is not automatically better, but you should know their limits.

3. **“Can you show me Marketplace/on-exchange plans as well as off-exchange plans?”**  
   Essential for individual/family coverage.

4. **“Are you paid by every carrier you recommend, and are there carriers you cannot sell?”**  
   Brokers are usually paid by carrier commissions; that is normal, but transparency matters.

5. **“Will you compare my doctors, hospital system, prescriptions, deductible, and maximum out-of-pocket cost?”**  
   In Kansas City, network access can be more important than a modest monthly-premium difference.

6. **“Can you send me the Summary of Benefits and Coverage and the provider-network link before I enroll?”**  
   Do not rely solely on a verbal network assurance.

7. **“Will you provide post-enrollment support if there is a billing, network, or claims issue?”**

## Verify before you buy

Before authorizing an application, verify the agent and agency through the relevant state regulator:

- **Kansas Insurance Department** — if you live on the Kansas side  
- **Missouri Department of Commerce and Insurance** — if you live on the Missouri side  

Also, never buy a plan described only as a “health-sharing program,” “limited benefit plan,” “fixed indemnity plan,” or “discount plan” unless you intentionally want something other than comprehensive major-medical insurance. Those products can be useful in narrow situations, but they are not substitutes for ACA-compliant coverage.

If you tell me your **ZIP code, age range, whether this is individual/family vs. employer vs. Medicare, preferred doctors/hospitals, and budget**, I can narrow this to the best broker type and the carriers/networks you should make sure they compare.
